sheet-101.description: The western end of Ventnor City at the Margate City line, sheet 101 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The part runs from Fredericksburg Avenue, along which the dash-dot Margate City boundary line is drawn, east to Melbourne Avenue and the edge of Pittsburg Avenue, and from Ventnor Avenue (80 ft) south across Atlantic Avenue (100 ft) to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean. Martindale, Washington, Swarthmore and Baltimore Avenues cross the sheet; below Atlantic Avenue a short Melbourne Place runs to the beach. The blocks between Ventnor and Atlantic Avenues are lotted and partly built with frame dwellings and private garages, most of them near Atlantic Avenue and on the Baltimore to Melbourne block. Atlantic Avenue carries the double tracks of the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (electric and steam) and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. The beach blocks south of Atlantic Avenue are lotted but empty; a narrow water course, coloured blue, crosses all of them about midway, and bulkhead lines are marked along Fredericksburg Avenue and Washington Avenue. Water pipes (4, 6, 8 and 12 inch) and hydrants are shown in the streets, with a note at Fredericksburg Avenue on an 8 inch connection to the Margate City water system, gate kept closed. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only; it is drawn on sheet 111.
notes: South Melbourne Avenue is printed with 'Park' in brackets.
Pittsburg Avenue is now Pittsburgh Avenue.
Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (electric and steam) and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad.
8 inch connection to the Margate City water system at Fredericksburg Avenue, gate kept closed.
street_widths Atlantic 100 ft and Ventnor 80 ft as labelled: without them the detector paired the Atlantic block line with the inner rail lines (residuals up to 7 m).

Sheet 101, 50 ft. One part: Fredericksburg (Margate City line) to Melbourne/Pittsburg Av, Ventnor Av to the Boardwalk; Martindale, Washington, Swarthmore, Baltimore; beach blocks empty with a water course. Pilot; street_widths Atlantic 100, Ventnor 80 (rails in Atlantic Av).

sheet-102.description: Western Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk, sheet 102 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Above Atlantic Avenue the part runs from the block west of Lafayette Avenue east to Wissahickon Avenue, crossing South Lafayette, South Wyoming, South Rosborough and Newark Avenues; several are lettered as parks ('Park', 'Margate Park'), the old names of the planned streets. Below Atlantic Avenue the beach streets are offset from those to the north: Pittsburg Avenue, Lafayette Place, Philadelphia Avenue, South Rosborough Avenue, South Newark Avenue and South Wissahickon Avenue run to a bulkhead line and the Boardwalk, with inclines at Philadelphia and Newark Avenues. The blocks north of Atlantic Avenue are built up with detached frame dwellings, many with brick-veneered first storeys, and private garages, more densely towards the east; a store and an auto basement stand on Wissahickon Avenue. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (electric and steam) and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. The beach blocks are lotted but almost empty, with three dwellings at Lafayette Place and one at South Newark Avenue; a blue water course crosses them, turning south to the bulkhead between Rosborough and Newark Avenues. A compass rose stands on the beach. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 112.
notes: South Lafayette and South Rosborough Avenues are printed with 'Park', South Wyoming Avenue with 'Margate Park', in brackets.
Pittsburg Avenue is now Pittsburgh Avenue.

The beach streets south of Atlantic Avenue (Pittsburg, Lafayette Place, Philadelphia) do not continue the avenues to the north; Lafayette Avenue and Lafayette Place meet Atlantic Avenue at separate junctions.
Inclines from the Boardwalk at Philadelphia and South Newark Avenues.
Sheet 102, 50 ft. One part: Lafayette to Wissahickon Av above Atlantic (Wyoming, Rosborough, Newark), offset beach streets Pittsburg, Lafayette Pl, Philadelphia below; water course on the beach.

sheet-103.description: Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from Wissahickon Avenue east to New Haven Avenue, sheet 103 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are South Wissahickon, South Buffalo, South Richards (40 ft) and South Troy Avenues, then a single large unbuilt block (block 70) reaching to South New Haven Avenue, with only two dwellings and a garage at its Troy Avenue end. The blocks from Wissahickon to Troy Avenue are closely built with detached frame dwellings, many with garages on their first storeys or behind, and some brick-veneered houses; the Richards to Troy block carries a row described as from plans. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (electric and steam) and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. South of Atlantic Avenue the beach blocks run to a bulkhead line, with inclines up to the Boardwalk at several street ends. Only South Avolyn Avenue is lettered there; the blocks between Wissahickon and Troy are partly built with dwellings, those to the east nearly empty. A blue water course enters at the west edge, turns south along the street at block 81B and curves across block 72A to the bulkhead, and the shore line steps south at the bulkhead east of Avolyn Avenue. A compass rose stands on the beach at the west. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 113.
notes: Avolyn Avenue is drawn only south of Atlantic Avenue; between Ventnor and Atlantic Avenues its line lies inside block 70 (the modern Avolyn / Ventnor junction is excluded).
The New Haven Avenue / Ventnor Avenue junction was not detected (sheet corner).
Sheet 103, 50 ft. One part: Wissahickon to New Haven Av (Buffalo, Richards, Troy); Avolyn only south of Atlantic (Avolyn/Ventnor excluded); water course on the beach.

sheet-104.description: Central Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from New Haven Avenue east to Sacramento Avenue, sheet 104 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are South Newport and South Portland Avenues, with a short Ocean Avenue between Portland and Sacramento Avenues. The sheet holds several institutions: the Jewish Seaside Home for Invalids with its annexes and a green house on the Newport to Portland block, St. James Roman Catholic Church on the same block towards Atlantic Avenue, and St. Johns by the Sea Episcopal Church with its parish house and rectory at Ventnor and Sacramento Avenues. Ventnor Avenue between New Haven and Newport Avenues is lined with stores and flats (some with three-storey frame buildings), and the rest of the blocks carry detached dwellings, many brick-veneered, and private garages. A trolley shelter shed stands on Atlantic Avenue below Ocean Avenue; Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (electric and steam) and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. South of Atlantic Avenue the large block 62 at the west end is empty and bounded by a bulkhead and a blue water line; east of it Stratford Place, South Princeton and South Sacramento Avenues lead to the bulkhead line and the Boardwalk, with inclines at the street ends, and the beach blocks there are built with dwellings, one marked as a foundation for a dwelling. A compass rose stands in block 62. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 114.
notes: Jewish Seaside Home for Invalids, with annexes and a green house, between Newport and Portland Avenues.
St. James Roman Catholic Church near Atlantic Avenue between Newport and Portland Avenues.
St. Johns by the Sea Episcopal Church, parish house and rectory at Ventnor and Sacramento Avenues.
Trolley shelter shed on Atlantic Avenue between Portland and Sacramento Avenues.
Only the north node of the two modern Newport Avenue / Atlantic Avenue nodes (15 m apart) is used; South Newport Avenue is not listed.
Sheet 104, 50 ft. One part: New Haven to Sacramento Av (Newport, Portland, Ocean Av; Stratford Pl, Princeton below Atlantic); Jewish Seaside Home for Invalids, St. James R.C., St. Johns by the Sea.

sheet-105.description: Central Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from Sacramento Avenue east past Cornwall Avenue, sheet 105 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the streets are South Sacramento Avenue, Madison Square (16), South Cambridge Avenue and South Cornwall Avenue (printed 'Av. (Pl.)'), with Ocean Avenue crossing from Sacramento to Cambridge Avenue; between Ocean and Atlantic Avenues lies a narrow open park. The blocks along Madison Square are closely built with detached dwellings, many with garages in their basements or first storeys, some with tile or brick-veneered first storeys; the larger blocks 43 and 40 east of Cambridge Avenue are more thinly built, with stuccoed and tile houses and garages. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (electric and steam). South of Atlantic Avenue South Sacramento, Harvard, South Cambridge and South Cornwall Avenues lead to the bulkhead line and the Boardwalk, with inclines at their ends; the beach blocks carry two- and three-storey dwellings and auto houses. Beyond the Boardwalk stand the Ventnor City Casino and Pier, with a hydrant and hose, and the Ventnor Fishing Pier running out into the ocean. A compass rose stands in the block west of Sacramento Avenue at Ocean Avenue. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 115.
notes: Madison Square, north of Atlantic Avenue, is now part of Harvard Avenue.
Ventnor City Casino and Pier, and the Ventnor Fishing Pier, off the Boardwalk at Cambridge Avenue.
A park fills the block between Ocean and Atlantic Avenues from Sacramento to Cambridge Avenue.
Sheet 105, 50 ft. One part: Sacramento to Cornwall Av (Madison Sq = Harvard Av, Cambridge, Ocean Av, park); Ventnor City Casino and Pier, Ventnor Fishing Pier.

sheet-106.description: Eastern Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from the block east of Cornwall Avenue to Dudley Avenue, sheet 106 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are lettered Derby Place, Dorset Place and Dudley Avenue (Place), each 56 ft 3 in wide; south of it they continue as South Derby, South Dorset and South Dudley Avenues to the bulkhead line and the Boardwalk, with inclines at their ends. The blocks are lotted in large residential lots and partly built with detached dwellings of two to three storeys, many of hollow tile or tile, some stuccoed or brick-veneered, with garages; foundations for tile buildings are marked on Ventnor Avenue between Derby and Dorset Places, and block 34 between Dorset and Dudley holds one large stuccoed dwelling. On the beach blocks two buildings are named, The Ardell and The Idlewylde (stuccoed), both west of South Derby Avenue. Atlantic Avenue is drawn without detail on this sheet beyond water pipes and hydrants. A compass rose stands east of Dudley Avenue. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 116.
notes: Derby Place and Dorset Place (north of Atlantic Avenue) are now Derby Avenue and Dorset Avenue.
The Ardell and The Idlewylde, beach-block buildings west of South Derby Avenue.
Foundations for tile buildings on Ventnor Avenue between Derby and Dorset Places.
Cornwall Avenue lies just off the west edge of the sheet; its junctions are not used.
Sheet 106, 50 ft. One part: Derby Pl, Dorset Pl, Dudley Av between Ventnor Av and the Boardwalk; Cornwall just off the west edge; six points.

sheet-107.description: Eastern Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from Dudley Avenue east to Suffolk Avenue, sheet 107 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are Dudley Avenue, Oxford Avenue (Place) and Somerset Avenue (Place), each 56 ft 3 in wide; south of it South Dudley, South Oxford, South Somerset and South Suffolk Avenues lead to the bulkhead line and the Boardwalk, with inclines at their ends. South Somerset Avenue lies well west of the line of Somerset Avenue north of Atlantic Avenue, so the beach blocks do not continue the blocks to the north. The blocks north of Atlantic Avenue (31, 28 and 25) are built with large detached dwellings of two to three storeys on big lots, several of hollow tile with cement coating or brick-veneered, with garages, brick and concrete fences 4 ft high, and on block 28 a large dwelling with a fire-proof garage of concrete floors and roof. On the beach, block 29 between South Oxford and South Somerset Avenues is closely built with dwellings; blocks 30 and 24 to either side are empty. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (electric and steam). A compass rose stands in block 25. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 117.
notes: Oxford and Somerset Avenues north of Atlantic Avenue are printed 'Av. (Pl.)'.
Somerset Avenue jogs at Atlantic Avenue: South Somerset meets it about 75 ft west of the northern part; the modern Atlantic / Somerset node fitted 5 m off and is excluded.
Blocks 30 and 24 on the beach are empty.
Sheet 107, 50 ft. One part: Dudley, Oxford, Somerset to Suffolk Av; Somerset jogs at Atlantic (Atlantic/Somerset excluded); six points.

sheet-108.description: Eastern Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from the block west of Suffolk Avenue east to Little Rock Avenue, sheet 108 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are Suffolk Avenue (Place), Surrey Avenue (Place), Victoria Avenue (60 ft) and Little Rock Avenue (50 ft); south of it South Suffolk, South Surrey, Victoria Avenue (Place) and South Little Rock Avenue lead to the bulkhead line and the Boardwalk, with inclines at the street ends. This is the business centre of Ventnor: along Atlantic Avenue between Surrey and Little Rock Avenues stand the Ventnor City National Bank, apartment buildings with stores, the post office, a drug store, a news office and, on the beach side at Victoria Avenue, the fireproof Ventnor Trust Company building with apartments. The residential blocks behind are closely built with two- to three-storey dwellings, many tile, hollow tile, stucco or brick-veneered, one under construction, with garages. On the beach block between South Surrey and Victoria Avenues stands the North American Sanitarium. The large block at the west end of the beach is empty apart from a compass rose, and a stone wall 3 ft high lines the bulkhead at South Suffolk Avenue. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (electric and steam). The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 118.
notes: Ventnor City National Bank, the post office and apartment buildings with stores on Atlantic Avenue between Surrey and Victoria Avenues.
Ventnor Trust Company (fireproof, with apartments) at Atlantic and Victoria Avenues, beach side.
North American Sanitarium on the beach block between South Surrey and Victoria Avenues.
Victoria Avenue jogs at Atlantic Avenue; the Atlantic / Victoria junction was 11 m off the fit and was rejected.

Sheet 108, 50 ft. One part: Suffolk, Surrey, Victoria, Little Rock Av; business centre (Ventnor City National Bank, post office, Ventnor Trust Co, North American Sanitarium); Atlantic/Victoria rejected (jog).

sheet-109.description: Eastern Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from Little Rock Avenue east to Oakland Avenue, sheet 109 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are South Weymouth Avenue (printed also as Florence Avenue), Frankfort Avenue, South Hillside Avenue, Nashville Avenue and South Oakland Avenue (64 ft); south of it South Little Rock, South Weymouth, South Frankfort, Amherst, South Nashville and South Oakland Avenues lead to the bulkhead and the Boardwalk, with inclines at their ends. Several beach streets are offset from the streets to the north: South Weymouth lies west of Weymouth Avenue, and Amherst Avenue takes the place of Hillside Avenue south of Atlantic Avenue. Ventnor Avenue between Little Rock and Weymouth Avenues is lined with stores, halls and flats, and at Weymouth Avenue a large public garage with cement floor and gasoline tanks; Atlantic Avenue at Little Rock Avenue has a drug store and apartments with stores. Otherwise the blocks are closely built with two- to four-storey detached dwellings, most of them brick-veneered on the first storey, with porches and garages, including one with a stone first storey. A concrete wall 4 ft high runs along the bulkhead west of South Weymouth Avenue, and the Boardwalk bends seaward at Frankfort Avenue. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (electric and steam). A compass rose stands on the beach at the east edge. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 119.
notes: South Weymouth Avenue is printed with '(Florence Av)'.
North Frankford Avenue is printed so on the top margin; the street is Frankfort Avenue.
Hillside Avenue (north of Atlantic Avenue) and Amherst Avenue (south of it) meet Atlantic Avenue about 57 ft apart; the single modern Amherst / Atlantic / Hillside node is excluded.
Public garage with gasoline tanks at Ventnor and Weymouth Avenues; stores and apartments at Ventnor and Little Rock Avenues and at Atlantic and Little Rock Avenues.
The Atlantic / Weymouth and Atlantic / Oakland junctions were not detected.
Sheet 109, 50 ft. One part: Little Rock to Oakland Av (Weymouth = Florence Av, Frankfort, Hillside/Amherst, Nashville); Hillside and Amherst meet Atlantic 57 ft apart (node excluded).

sheet-110.description: The eastern end of the Ventnor City beach front, between Ventnor Avenue and the Boardwalk from Oakland Avenue east to Jackson Avenue, the boundary with Atlantic City, sheet 110 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are South Oakland Avenue (64 ft), Austin Avenue, Marion Avenue, Baton Rouge Avenue and Vassar Square, each 50 ft; south of Atlantic Avenue South Oakland, South Austin, Marion, South Baton Rouge, South Vassar and South Jackson Avenues run down to the bulkhead and end in inclines to the Boardwalk. South Oakland and Marion Avenues are offset to the east south of Atlantic Avenue. Jackson Avenue (50 ft) carries the dash-dot city line, lettered Ventnor on one side and Atlantic City on the other; the gate on the 6 inch water pipe at Ventnor Avenue is noted as kept closed. The blocks are almost entirely residential: two- to four-storey frame dwellings, many with brick, tile or stucco first storeys, porches and private garages, with a row of four houses facing Atlantic Avenue at Marion Avenue, two apartment houses at Atlantic Avenue and Vassar Square and a pair of iron-clad stores near Jackson Avenue. Much of the westernmost block and the southern ends of the beach blocks are still vacant. A concrete retaining wall 6 ft high runs along the bulkhead. Atlantic Avenue (100 ft) carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (electric and steam) and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. A compass rose stands in South Oakland Avenue at the west edge. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 120.
notes: Jackson Avenue is the boundary between Ventnor and Atlantic City; the adjoining Atlantic City sheet is 53.
South Oakland Avenue and Marion Avenue jog about 45 ft east at Atlantic Avenue; the single modern Atlantic / Oakland and Atlantic / Marion nodes are excluded.
Two apartment houses and two iron-clad stores at Atlantic Avenue between Vassar Square and Jackson Avenue.
The Marion / Ventnor junction was not detected.
Sheet 110, 50 ft. Beach row Oakland Av to Jackson Av (Atlantic City line), Ventnor Av to Boardwalk; Oakland and Marion jog at Atlantic Av (excluded). One part.

sheet-111.description: The western end of Ventnor City on the bay side of Ventnor Avenue, at the Margate City line, sheet 111 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North Fredericksburg Avenue on the west edge carries the dash-dot boundary line between Margate City and Ventnor. South of Winchester Avenue the cross streets are North Martindale, North Washington, North Swarthmore and North Baltimore Avenues (50 ft) and North Melbourne Avenue (60 ft), with Ventnor Avenue cut along the bottom edge. North of Winchester Avenue most of the ground is two large undivided blocks (112 and 105), crossed by a winding arm of the Inside Thoroughfare with a single dwelling on piles at its edge; North Baltimore and North Melbourne Avenues continue to Monmouth Avenue at the top right, where the Thoroughfare shore turns along block 104. At the top left a paper subdivision is outlined: Arctic Avenue and a North Washington Avenue and North Swarthmore Avenue drawn on a slightly different alignment from the streets below, with blocks 60, 61 and 67 divided into lots but unbuilt. The lots south of Winchester Avenue are also divided but almost empty: a handful of one- and two-storey frame dwellings with private garages on North Washington, North Swarthmore and North Baltimore Avenues, a few dwellings on Monmouth Avenue and an iron garage standing alone in block 105. The north side of Ventnor Avenue only is shown; the beach side is on sheet 101. Margate City continues on sheet 136.
notes: North Fredericksburg Avenue carries the boundary line between Margate City and Ventnor.

Arctic Avenue and the North Washington and North Swarthmore Avenues north of it at the top left are a platted subdivision on a different alignment from the streets south of Winchester Avenue; no modern junction is used there, and the modern Monmouth Avenue junctions with Washington, Swarthmore and Martindale Avenues are excluded.
The Martindale / Winchester junction is detected where drawn but its modern reference lies about 8 m off the fit; it was rejected.
Ventnor Avenue is cut at about its centreline along the bottom edge.
Sheet 111, 50 ft. Bay side at the Margate line, Fredericksburg to Melbourne Av, Ventnor to Monmouth Av; top left is a platted subdivision (Arctic Av) on its own alignment, not used. One part.

sheet-112.description: Bay-side blocks of western Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Inside Thoroughfare, from North Melbourne Avenue east to North Wissahickon Avenue, sheet 112 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Winchester Avenue and Monmouth Avenue cross the sheet; the cross streets are North Melbourne, North Lafayette, North Wyoming, North Rosborough, North Newark and North Wissahickon Avenues, all 60 ft wide. North of Winchester Avenue the cross streets are lettered only as '(Park) Av.', and North Wyoming Avenue as 'Av. (Margate Park)'. Beyond Monmouth Avenue a row of shallow blocks (96, 95, 87, 86) backs onto the Inside Thoroughfare, whose shore runs along the top edge and bends south-east at the right. The area is laid out in lots but thinly built: scattered two- and three-storey frame dwellings, several with brick first storeys and private garages, set more closely near Ventnor Avenue, where four small houses face the avenue at North Wyoming Avenue. On North Lafayette Avenue near Monmouth Avenue stands a large public garage of 30, 20 and 12 car capacity with cement floors and electric light, with a gasoline tank across the street; a concrete-block dwelling stands in block 88. Most of block 97 and the lots north of Winchester Avenue are empty. Ventnor Avenue is cut along the bottom edge and its beach side is drawn on sheet 102; sheets 111 and 113 adjoin on the west and east.
notes: North of Winchester Avenue the cross streets carry a parenthesised '(Park)' and North Wyoming Avenue '(Margate Park)', apparently earlier development names.
Public garage of 30, 20 and 12 car capacity on North Lafayette Avenue near Monmouth Avenue.
Ventnor Avenue is cut at about its centreline along the bottom edge.
Sheet 112, 50 ft. Melbourne to Wissahickon Av, Ventnor Av to Inside Thoroughfare; streets north of Winchester printed "(Park) Av.". One part.

sheet-113.description: Bay-side blocks of central Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Inside Thoroughfare, from North Wissahickon Avenue east to North New Haven Avenue, sheet 113 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Winchester Avenue and Monmouth Avenue cross the sheet; the cross streets are North Wissahickon, North Buffalo, North Richards, North Troy, North Avolyn and North New Haven Avenues. North Troy and North New Haven Avenues and Winchester Avenue east of North Troy are 80 ft wide around the civic block 69, the others 50 ft. Block 69, from North Troy to North New Haven Avenue south of Winchester Avenue, holds the Troy Avenue Public School (two storeys, tile walls with brick facing, concrete floors, electric light and steam heat) and Ventnor City Hall with the city offices and the fire department, whose equipment of a paid and volunteer company, pumping engines, a chemical truck and an aerial truck is listed in a note; North Avolyn Avenue does not continue south of Winchester Avenue. The other blocks are divided into narrow lots and partly built with one- and two-storey dwellings, many with garages in the basement or brick and tile first storeys; blocks 78A and 75B north of Winchester Avenue are almost empty, and block 75B is vacant. Beyond Monmouth Avenue a row of shallow lots (blocks 77, 76, 67) backs onto the Inside Thoroughfare, with a boat slip cut into the shore. A compass rose stands at the upper left. Ventnor Avenue is cut along the bottom edge; its beach side is on sheet 103.
notes: Troy Avenue Public School and Ventnor City Hall with the Ventnor Fire Department occupy block 69.
North Avolyn Avenue ends at Winchester Avenue; the modern Avolyn / Ventnor junction is excluded.
Winchester Avenue, North Troy Avenue and North New Haven Avenue are drawn 80 ft wide around block 69.
Ventnor Avenue is cut along the bottom edge; the Ventnor / Wissahickon and Monmouth / Wissahickon junctions were not detected.
Sheet 113, 50 ft. Wissahickon to New Haven Av; Troy Ave Public School and City Hall in block 69 (Avolyn ends at Winchester). One part.

sheet-114.description: Bay-side blocks of central Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and Monmouth Avenue, from North New Haven Avenue east to North Sacramento Avenue, sheet 114 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Winchester Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet. North of it the cross streets are Bryant, North Newport, North Portland and North Princeton Avenues, with North New Haven and North Sacramento Avenues on the edges; south of Winchester Avenue only North Newport and North Portland Avenues continue to Ventnor Avenue, and blocks 64, 59 and 54 run the full width between them. Beyond Monmouth Avenue the top row of blocks (66, 57, 56) is outlined only and drawn on sheet 121. The district is residential: two- and three-storey frame dwellings, many with tile or brick first storeys and basement garages, including a uniform row of tile-fronted houses on both sides of block 65A, a row of five houses on Winchester Avenue in block 59, the Newport Apartments of tile construction in block 64 and an apartment house drawn from plans at North New Haven Avenue. Small trades appear among them: a carpenter shop with electric power in block 58 and a plumber shop with an office and private garage in block 54. Stores face Ventnor Avenue in block 59. Much of block 58 and most of block 54 are still vacant lots. A compass rose stands in block 66. Ventnor Avenue runs along the bottom edge; its beach side is on sheet 104.
notes: Bryant Avenue and North Princeton Avenue end at Winchester Avenue; blocks 64 and 54 run through to Ventnor Avenue.
Newport Apartments (tile construction) in block 64; an apartment house at North New Haven Avenue is drawn from plans.
The New Haven Avenue junctions lie just off the west edge and are placed from the drawn east edge of the street; the Sacramento / Ventnor junction was not detected.
Sheet 114, 50 ft. New Haven to Sacramento Av, Ventnor to Monmouth Av; Bryant and Princeton end at Winchester. One part.

sheet-115.description: Bay-side blocks of central Ventnor City from North Sacramento Avenue east to North Derby Place and the Inside Thoroughfare, between Ventnor Avenue and Monmouth Avenue, sheet 115 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The cross streets are North Sacramento, North Harvard (printed also as Brockley Avenue), North Cambridge and North Cornwall Avenues. Winchester Avenue jogs at Cornwall: west of it it runs across the middle of the sheet, east of it about 230 ft further south, and the two are joined by a southern section of Cornwall printed 'Av. (Pl.)', which lies about 150 ft east of North Cornwall Avenue (40 ft) north of Winchester Avenue. Block 45A, between North Cornwall Avenue and the Inside Thoroughfare, holds the Ventnor Water Works: a pump house with wood roof on iron trusses and concrete floor, a brick chimney 100 ft high, a stand pipe of 190,300 gallons, a concrete reservoir of 800,000 gallons, a shop, a storage house, a sewer motor house and a sewer pump house and vault; a note gives one McGowen pump of 3,500,000 and two Worthington pumps of 1,500,000 gallons a day. Along the Thoroughfare shore stand dwellings whose rear ends rest on piling. The other blocks are residential, with one- to three-storey frame dwellings, many stuccoed or with brick or tile first storeys, and private garages; block 44 is still largely vacant. A creek enters at the top right, and the top row of blocks beyond Monmouth Avenue is drawn on sheet 121. Ventnor Avenue runs along the bottom edge; its beach side is on sheet 105.
notes: North Harvard Avenue is printed with '(Brockley Av.)'; it is Harvard Avenue today.

Winchester Avenue jogs about 230 ft south at Cornwall Avenue, and North Cornwall Avenue north of Winchester lies about 150 ft west of the Cornwall section south of it (printed 'Av. (Pl.)'); all three modern Cornwall / Winchester nodes match drawn junctions.
Ventnor Water Works with pump house, 100 ft brick chimney, stand pipe and an 800,000 gallon concrete reservoir in block 45A.
The Derby / Winchester junction (two modern nodes about 25 m apart) is excluded; Harvard / Ventnor and Derby / Ventnor were not detected.
Fitted scale 8.10 px/ft, about 1 percent above the neighbouring sheets.
Sheet 115, 50 ft. Sacramento Av to Derby Pl; Ventnor Water Works; Winchester jogs south at Cornwall, North Harvard printed "(Brockley Av.)". One part.

sheet-116.description: The crossing of the Inside Thoroughfare between Ventnor City and Ventnor Heights, from North Derby Place east to North Dudley Avenue, sheet 116 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The bottom third shows the bay-side blocks between Ventnor Avenue and Winchester Avenue at North Derby Place, North Dorset Place (56 ft) and North Dudley Avenue, printed 'Av. (Pl.)'; Winchester Avenue does not cross block 33 between Dorset and Dudley and runs on at a different line east of North Dudley Avenue. North of these blocks the shore of the Inside Thoroughfare is lined with bulkheads. Grand Avenue (80 ft) crosses the Thoroughfare to North Dorset Place on an iron bridge with plank floor and a draw section. The upper half shows the first blocks of Ventnor Heights, laid out between Avenue A along the shore and Avenue B at the top, with 5th Avenue curving round to meet Avenue A at Grand Avenue, and 6th and 7th Avenues; blocks 113, 114 and 115 are divided into narrow lots, sparsely built with frame and concrete dwellings, private garages and the two-storey Faith Tabernacle (stove heat, electric and gas light). Along the curved shore of 5th Avenue and along Avenue A stand dwellings and boat houses whose rears rest on piles over the water, with boats housed underneath. To the west the Thoroughfare widens into an open basin with three small piers on its far shore. The north side of Ventnor Avenue is drawn here; its beach side is on sheet 106.
notes: Ventnor Heights street names of 1921 and the modern names: Avenue A is Edgewater Avenue, Avenue B is Monmouth Avenue, 5th Avenue is North Derby Avenue, Grand Avenue is Dorset Avenue, 6th Avenue is North Dudley Avenue, 7th Avenue is Oxford Avenue.
Iron bridge with plank floor and draw section carries Grand Avenue across the Inside Thoroughfare to North Dorset Place.
Faith Tabernacle in block 114.
Winchester Avenue jogs at North Derby Place (two modern nodes about 25 m apart, both drawn) and is interrupted by block 33 between North Dorset Place and North Dudley Avenue.
The five-way Dorset / Edgewater / North Derby junction (Grand Avenue, Avenue A and the end of the 5th Avenue curve) is excluded; with it the fit was 1.24 m, without it 0.84 m.
The fitted rotation (31.2 degrees) is about one degree less than on the neighbouring bay-side sheets.

Sheet 116, 50 ft. Ventnor Heights (Avenue A/B, 5th, Grand, 6th, 7th Av) across the Inside Thoroughfare from the Derby-Dudley bay-side blocks; iron bridge on Grand Av. One part (drawn in one frame, checked).

sheet-117.description: Both shores of the Inside Thoroughfare between North Dudley and North Somerset Avenues, sheet 117 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The upper half shows Ventnor Heights between Avenue B at the top and Avenue A along the water, with 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th Avenues (50 ft); blocks 116, 117 and 118 are divided into narrow lots and stand empty apart from one dwelling at Avenue A and 8th Avenue. Along the north shore, below Avenue A, a strip of lots (block 185) carries a few dwellings on posts over the water with motor boats underneath, and a wharf. The broad Inside Thoroughfare fills the middle of the sheet, with a compass rose and the scale of feet. On the south shore, between the water and Winchester Avenue, a row of shallow lots (blocks 32, 27 and 26) is built with small dwellings on posts, open underneath or with boat slips and motor boats beneath. South of Winchester Avenue, between North Dudley (56 ft 3 in), North Oxford and North Somerset Avenues, block 32 holds the Oxford Avenue Public School, a two-storey building with steam heat and electric and gas light, and blocks 27 and 26 hold one- and two-storey frame dwellings, some stuccoed or tiled, with private garages. Ventnor Avenue runs along the bottom edge; its beach side is on sheet 107. Sheets 116 and 118 adjoin along the shore line.
notes: Ventnor Heights names of 1921 and the modern names: Avenue A is Edgewater Avenue, Avenue B is Monmouth Avenue, 7th Avenue is Oxford Avenue, 8th Avenue is Somerset Avenue, 10th Avenue is Surrey Avenue; 9th Avenue has no named modern way in the reference data.
Oxford Avenue Public School in block 32.
Dwellings on posts over the Inside Thoroughfare on both shores, with motor boats underneath.
Fitted scale 8.13 px/ft and rotation 31.2 degrees, about 1.5 percent and one degree off the bay-side sheets 111 to 114; the fit is consistent (0.8 m) across both shores.
Sheet 117, 50 ft. Ventnor Heights (Avenue A/B, 7th-10th Av) across the Inside Thoroughfare from Dudley-Somerset bay-side blocks; Oxford Ave Public School. One part.

sheet-118.description: Bay side of Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Inside Thoroughfare from west of North Suffolk Avenue east to North Little Rock Avenue, with the mouth of the East Canal and the southern edge of Ventnor Heights above it, sheet 118 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. South of the thoroughfare the cross streets are North Suffolk Avenue, North Surrey Avenue (printed also as Surrey Place), North Victoria Avenue and North Little Rock Avenue. Winchester Avenue steps north at Surrey Avenue: west of it it runs about 230 ft from Ventnor Avenue, east of it along the bulkhead about 350 ft from it. The blocks hold two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, several stuccoed or with tile roofs, with automobile basements and private garages; along the bulkhead west of Surrey Avenue are a pavilion, boat houses and dwellings with motor boats underneath, on posts over the water. North of the thoroughfare the East Canal runs up the left half of the sheet. On its west bank, 10th Avenue with Avenue A meeting it at the left edge, a row of small dwellings and boat houses on posts occupies lots of block 192. East of the canal the unbuilt Ventnor Heights blocks 33, 34, 38, 39 and 194 are laid out along Columbus Avenue and Mediterranean Avenue, both marked not open, with Park Avenue at the top edge; their southern edge follows the curving shore of the thoroughfare. A compass rose and the scale of feet stand in the open water. The south side of Ventnor Avenue is drawn on sheet 108.
notes: 10th Avenue of the Ventnor Heights plan is the northern part of today's Surrey Avenue, and Avenue A is Edgewater Avenue; their junction fits the modern node to 1 m.
The East Canal has been filled; Columbus Avenue and Mediterranean Avenue (not open) were never built on the lines drawn.
North Surrey Avenue is printed with '(Pl.)'; Winchester Avenue jogs at Surrey Avenue, matching the two modern Surrey / Winchester nodes.
Ventnor Avenue lies at the bottom edge; its junctions were placed from the drawn north edge (boundary street).
Fitted rotation 33.6 degrees, about one degree more than the neighbouring sheets; the drawn Ventnor Avenue edge is tilted the same way on the scan.

Sheet 118, 50 ft. N. Suffolk to N. Little Rock, Ventnor to Winchester (jogs at Surrey); above the thoroughfare East Canal mouth, 10th Av (= Surrey) / Avenue A (= Edgewater), Columbus and Mediterranean Av (not open). One part.

sheet-119.description: Bay side of eastern Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Inside Thoroughfare, from North Little Rock Avenue east to North Oakland Avenue, sheet 119 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The cross streets are North Little Rock Avenue, North Weymouth Avenue (printed also as North Florence Avenue), North Frankfort Avenue, North Hillside Avenue, North Nashville Avenue and North Oakland Avenue, all 50 ft wide, running from Ventnor Avenue (80 ft) north to Winchester Avenue. Winchester Avenue follows the bulkhead of the Inside Thoroughfare; west of Weymouth Avenue it steps south, and a short length of it is lettered between Little Rock and Weymouth Avenues. The blocks are closely built with two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, most with automobile basements, and private garages. Ventnor Avenue carries stores, among them a row of tile-roofed stores at Little Rock Avenue, and the First Congregational Church stands at the corner of Frankfort and Ventnor Avenues; an apartment house and a brick dwelling stand near Oakland Avenue. Along the water side of Winchester Avenue are boat houses, motor boat slips and dwellings with motor boats underneath, built out over the bulkhead. North of the Inside Thoroughfare the sheet shows unbuilt Ventnor Heights lots of block 39 and 40, cut by Frankfort Avenue and Nashville Avenue (not open) and bounded by Mediterranean Avenue (not open), which belong to the 100 ft sheet 126. A compass rose stands in the thoroughfare at the east side. The south side of Ventnor Avenue is outlined only and drawn on sheet 109.
notes: North Weymouth Avenue is printed with '(N. Florence)'.
Mediterranean Avenue and the Ventnor Heights parts of Frankfort and Nashville Avenues are marked 'not open'; they were never built and the area is not in the modern street network.
North Oakland Avenue meets Ventnor Avenue offset from South Oakland Avenue; the modern Oakland / Ventnor node is excluded.
First Congregational Church at Frankfort and Ventnor Avenues.
Sheet 119, 50 ft. N. Little Rock to N. Oakland, Ventnor to Winchester; Mediterranean Av (not open) above the thoroughfare. Oakland offset at Ventnor (excluded).

sheet-120.description: Bay side of easternmost Ventnor City between Ventnor Avenue and the Inside Thoroughfare, from North Oakland Avenue east to North Jackson Avenue, the Atlantic City line, sheet 120 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. South of the thoroughfare the cross streets are North Oakland Avenue, North Austin Avenue, Dilks Avenue, North Baton Rouge Avenue, North Vassar Square (printed also as Lincoln Avenue) and North Jackson Avenue, with Callender Avenue (35 ft) running across the blocks a short way north of Ventnor Avenue. Winchester Avenue is drawn only at the west end, between Oakland and Austin Avenues; east of Austin Avenue the blocks run up to the bulkhead. Building is lighter than further west: two-storey frame dwellings with automobile basements and private garages fill the block between Oakland and Austin Avenues and part of the blocks east of Baton Rouge Avenue, while the blocks around Dilks Avenue are subdivided but mostly empty. A large public garage for 100 cars, with concrete floor, steam heat, electric light and a roof on iron trusses, stands on Callender Avenue at Baton Rouge Avenue, with a buried gasoline tank beside it; a stuccoed dwelling and small stores face Ventnor Avenue. The Atlantic City line runs along Jackson Avenue, and the Atlantic City sheet 57 is referred to beyond it. North of the Inside Thoroughfare the sheet shows the unbuilt Ventnor Heights plan at the same scale: Mediterranean Avenue, Nashville, Austin, Lancaster, Baton Rouge and Jackson Avenues and Boulevard, all marked not open, with lots of blocks 41, 42, 84, 85 and 89. A compass rose stands in the thoroughfare at the west side. The south side of Ventnor Avenue is drawn on sheet 110.
notes: Dilks Avenue is now Marion Avenue; its junctions with Callender and Ventnor Avenues fitted about 12 m off the modern nodes and were rejected (Marion Avenue south of Ventnor Avenue is printed so).
North Vassar Square is printed with '(Lincoln Av.)'; the modern name is Vassar Square.

The Ventnor Heights streets north of the thoroughfare (Mediterranean, Lancaster, Boulevard and the northern ends of Austin, Baton Rouge and Jackson Avenues) are marked not open and do not exist today.
Public garage for 100 cars at Callender and Baton Rouge Avenues.
City line of Ventnor and Atlantic City along Jackson Avenue.
Sheet 120, 50 ft. N. Oakland to N. Jackson (city line), Callender Av; Dilks Av (= Marion, 12 m off, rejected); unbuilt Heights above the thoroughfare. One part.

sheet-121.description: Western Ventnor Heights between the West Canal and Grand Avenue, with the Inside Thoroughfare and the north side of Monmouth Avenue below it, sheet 121 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The Heights are a paper subdivision of long narrow lots in blocks 125 to 129, 135 to 139 and 145 to 149, laid out on 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Avenues and Grand Avenue (80 ft) running up the sheet and Avenue C, Avenue D and Avenue E across it, all marked not open; Park Avenue at the top edge borders a parkway of oval plots continued on sheet 123, and block 187 lines the east bank of the West Canal. The only buildings north of the thoroughfare stand along Avenue C at the water: a strip of boat houses and small dwellings over the water in block 186, and at its east end the Ventnor Boat Works, with a repair shop and painting shed, no watchman, power and lights by electricity and heat by stoves. Below Avenue C, along 5th Avenue and down to Avenue B, blocks 186 and 119 hold a few dwellings with automobile basements and motor boat houses on the water. South of the thoroughfare the sheet shows the north ends of North Newport, North Portland, North Sacramento and North Cambridge Avenues with blocks 57, 56, 47 and 46, a few dwellings and motor boat houses on the shore, and Monmouth Avenue at the bottom edge with North Princeton, North Harvard and North Cornwall Avenues leaving it to the south. A compass rose and the scale of feet stand in the blank area west of the canal, which belongs to no sheet.
notes: The Ventnor Heights plan survives in today's street grid under other names: 1st Avenue is Harvard Avenue, 2nd Cambridge, 3rd Cornwall, 4th Burghley, 5th Derby and Grand Avenue Dorset Avenue; Avenue B is Monmouth Avenue, C Calvert, D Balfour and E Fremont Avenue. All junctions fit the modern nodes to within 3 m.
The Inside Thoroughfare between Avenue C and Monmouth Avenue and the West Canal have since been filled.
Today's Fulton Avenue runs down the middle of the parkway between the two Park Avenues; its junctions were not used.
Ventnor Boat Works at Avenue C and 5th Avenue.

Sheet 121, 100 ft. Ventnor Heights west: 1st-5th, Grand Av = Harvard, Cambridge, Cornwall, Burghley, Derby, Dorset; Avenues B-E = Monmouth, Calvert, Balfour, Fremont. West Canal; Monmouth Av row at bottom.

sheet-122.description: Central Ventnor Heights between Grand Avenue and the East Canal, from Park Avenue south to Avenue B, sheet 122 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The sheet is almost entirely a paper subdivision: blocks 120 to 124, 130 to 134, 140 to 144 and 150 to 154 of long narrow lots laid out on Grand Avenue (80 ft) and 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th Avenues running up the sheet, and Avenue E, Avenue D, Avenue C and Avenue B across it, all 50 ft and marked not open. Block 192, a single row of lots, lines the west bank of the East Canal, which runs the full height of the sheet on the right. At the top Park Avenue borders a parkway of oval plots shared with sheets 121 and 124. The only buildings are a handful of one- and two-storey dwellings with automobile basements in block 120 along Grand Avenue, a stuccoed dwelling with tile roof and two small dwellings in block 121 near Avenue B, and two dwellings in block 192 by the canal. At the bottom right, beyond the canal, a corner of Park Avenue and Columbus Avenue (not open) belongs to sheet 118. The right part of the sheet beyond the canal is blank apart from the sheet references 125 and 126, the title and a compass rose; the scale of feet stands at the bottom.
notes: The plan survives in today's grid: Grand Avenue is Dorset Avenue, 6th Avenue Dudley, 7th Oxford, 8th Somerset and 10th Avenue the northern part of Surrey Avenue; Avenue B is Monmouth, C Calvert, D Balfour and E Fremont Avenue. 9th Avenue has no modern counterpart (Burk Court lies on its line further north).
The East Canal has been filled; Victoria and Little Rock Avenues now cross its site.

Avenue B is drawn about 52 ft wide; with the parcel width the detector paired its north edge with a lot line 45 ft inside the blocks, so its width is set to 54 ft. Two Monmouth Avenue junctions were still rejected.
Sheet 122, 100 ft. Heights Grand-10th Av (= Dorset, Dudley, Oxford, Somerset, -, Surrey), Avenue B-E, East Canal. Monmouth width set to 54.

sheet-123.description: Northwestern Ventnor Heights between the West Canal and Grand Avenue, from Park Avenue north to the Beach Thoroughfare, sheet 123 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The sheet shows an unbuilt subdivision only: blocks 155 to 159, 165 to 169 and 175 to 179 of long narrow lots, laid out on 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Avenues (50 ft) and Grand Avenue (80 ft) running up the sheet and Avenue F, Avenue G and Avenue H across it, every street marked not opened. Block 188, a single row of lots, lines the east bank of the West Canal, and block 189 runs along the bulkhead of the Beach Thoroughfare at the top, with a small boat basin cut into it at the east end. At the bottom two Park Avenues enclose a parkway of oval plots with circles at their ends, continued on sheets 121, 122 and 124. No building is drawn anywhere on the sheet. The area west of the canal is blank apart from the title, the scale note, a compass rose and the scale of feet, and the West Canal itself runs the full height of the sheet from the Beach Thoroughfare southward.
notes: The plan survives in today's grid: 1st Avenue is Harvard Avenue, 2nd Cambridge, 3rd Cornwall, 4th Burghley, 5th Derby and Grand Avenue Dorset Avenue; Avenue F is Wellington Avenue, G Marshall Avenue and H Burk Avenue.
Today's Fulton Avenue runs down the parkway between the two Park Avenues.
The West Canal has been filled; the shore of the Beach Thoroughfare has moved since.
Two Wellington Avenue junctions paired a lot line until the street width was set to the drawn 50 ft; Dorset Avenue is set to the drawn 80 ft.
Sheet 123, 100 ft. Heights NW: 1st-5th, Grand; Avenues F, G, H = Wellington, Marshall, Burk; Park Av parkway (Fulton runs down it); West Canal, Beach Thoroughfare.

sheet-124.description: Northern Ventnor Heights between Grand Avenue and the East Canal, from Park Avenue north to the Beach Thoroughfare, with a strip of the subdivision east of the canal, sheet 124 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The sheet shows an unbuilt subdivision only: blocks 160 to 164, 170 to 174 and 180 to 184 of long narrow lots, laid out on Grand Avenue (80 ft) and 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th Avenues (50 ft) running up the sheet and Avenue F, Avenue G and Avenue H across it; the avenues are marked not opened and the lettered ones also not named. Block 190 runs along the bulkhead of the Beach Thoroughfare at the top, with a boat basin cut in at its west end, and block 191 lines the west bank of the East Canal. Two Park Avenues and their parkway of oval plots cross the bottom of the sheet. East of the canal, block 193 lines the opposite bank, and beyond it lie blocks 1, 6, 7, 12 and 13 of the next subdivision, cut by St. Augustine Avenue, Baylor Avenue (both not opened) and a street lettered not named, drawn at a slight angle to the Heights grid and continued on sheet 125; their northern end follows a winding creek bank. No building is drawn on the sheet. A compass rose stands in the thoroughfare at the top left, and the scale of feet at the bottom right.
notes: The plan survives in today's grid: Grand Avenue is Dorset Avenue, 6th Avenue Dudley, 7th Oxford, 8th Somerset and 10th Avenue Surrey Avenue; Avenue F is Wellington Avenue, G Marshall and H Burk Avenue. 9th Avenue has no modern counterpart.
The East Canal has been filled; modern Little Rock Avenue runs along its east bank. St. Augustine and Baylor Avenues were never built.
The junction of 10th Avenue and Avenue G (Surrey / Marshall) was detected 21 ft off the drawn centre and is excluded.
Sheet 124, 100 ft. Heights N: Grand-10th Av, Avenues F-H; East Canal; strip east of the canal (St. Augustine, Baylor, not built) in the same frame. One part.

sheet-125.description: Northeastern Ventnor Heights between North Little Rock Avenue and North Jackson Avenue, from the Beach Thoroughfare south to Crossan Avenue, sheet 125 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The whole sheet is an unbuilt paper subdivision with no buildings drawn. Two street grids meet on it. In the west, North Little Rock, North Frankfort, North Nashville and North Austin Avenues run up the sheet at a slight angle, crossed by St. Augustine Avenue, Baylor Avenue, Ferdinand Avenue and Alden Avenue, with blocks 1 to 5, 7 to 11, 13 to 17 and 18 to 23 of long narrow lots. In the east, Lancaster Avenue, North Baton Rouge Avenue and North Jackson Avenue (80 ft) run straight up the sheet, crossed by John, Elizabeth, West End and Crossan Avenues, with blocks 1, 2, 3 and 6, 7, 8 and 20, 21, 22; nearly every street is marked not opened. A row of lots, block 1, lines the bulkhead of the Beach Thoroughfare along John Avenue, and the shore of the thoroughfare winds across the top left corner, where a compass rose stands in the water. Sheet 91 of the Atlantic City volume is referred to beyond Jackson Avenue, sheets 124 and 122 at the left and 126 below. The scale of feet stands at the bottom left.
notes: None of the streets on this sheet was built; the area has no modern street junctions. The sheet is placed by four block corners on the west side of Little Rock Avenue (blocks 7 and 13 at St. Augustine and Baylor Avenues) carried from sheet 124, which draws the same strip east of the East Canal (helmert fit, low confidence).

Check: the drawn junction of West End and Jackson Avenues lands about 8 m from the line of today's West End Avenue / Wellington Avenue and about 25 m east of the modern Jackson Avenue line; sheet 120 draws the Heights Jackson Avenue about 17 m east of that line, so the placement agrees with sheet 120 to about 8 m.
West End, Crossan and Elizabeth Avenues continued the streets of Chelsea Heights in Atlantic City; today Wellington Avenue follows the West End Avenue line.

Sheet 125, 100 ft. Heights NE, unbuilt (Little Rock-Austin tilted grid; Lancaster-Jackson with John, Elizabeth, West End, Crossan). Helmert from four block corners on Little Rock Av carried from sheet 124 (the strip east of the East Canal drawn on both); low confidence.

sheet-126.description: Eastern Ventnor Heights between Frankfort Avenue and North Jackson Avenue, from Crossan Avenue south to Mediterranean Avenue above the Inside Thoroughfare, sheet 126 of the Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The whole sheet is an unbuilt paper subdivision with no buildings drawn. In the west, Frankfort, North Nashville and North Austin Avenues run up the sheet at a slight angle, crossed by Carlton, Adriatic and Caspian Avenues, Park Avenue and Mediterranean Avenue, with blocks 21 to 37 of long narrow lots. In the east, Lancaster Avenue, North Baton Rouge Avenue and North Jackson Avenue run straight up the sheet, crossed by Crossan, Filbert, Porter and King Avenues, with blocks 36 to 38, 52 to 54 and 68 to 70; the junction between the two grids runs diagonally down the middle of the sheet. Every street is marked not opened. A strip along the left edge is blank, with the sheet reference 122; sheets 125 above, 118, 119 and 120 below and Atlantic City sheet 91 to the right are referred to. A compass rose stands at the bottom left and the scale of feet at the bottom right.
notes: None of the streets on this sheet was built; the area has no modern street junctions. The sheet is placed by ten block corners: four on the north side of Mediterranean Avenue carried from sheets 119 and 120 and six on Crossan Avenue carried from sheet 125 (itself placed from sheet 124); a first-order fit at 0.8 m RMSE, low confidence since no point is a modern junction.
Check: the drawn junction of Filbert and Jackson Avenues lands about 9 m from the line of today's Filbert Avenue in Atlantic City extended west.
Crossan, Filbert and Porter Avenues continued the streets of Chelsea Heights in Atlantic City, where they exist today.

Sheet 126, 100 ft. Heights E, unbuilt (Frankfort-Austin tilted grid; Lancaster-Jackson with Crossan, Filbert, Porter, King). First-order fit on ten block corners: Mediterranean Av from sheets 119/120 and Crossan Av from sheet 125; low confidence.
